title: carex fusca var. intricata
intro: Carex fusca var. intricata, commonly known as  lesser purple sedge, is a type of flowering plant in the sedge family. It is native to the Pacific Northwest region of North America. The health benefits of Carex fusca var. intricata include its use in traditional medicine to treat fever, rheumatism, and skin conditions, due to its anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties. The plant contains bioactive constituents such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, including antioxidant, antimicrobial, and anti-inflammatory effects.
